rules.title: Rules
rules.description: After every sync or import, each enabled rule completes all the transactions it targets, older ones included: category, merchant, tag, name, activity label, exclusion or expected transfer. A new rule stays disabled until you confirm it should apply to existing transactions. Rules apply in the order they were created, whatever the list is sorted by, and each one sees what the previous ones changed. When two rules change the same field, the last one wins; a tag is added to the others. A field you edited by hand is never replaced.

prompt.description: You can create a rule to automatically categorize transactions like this one
prompt.hideForTodayHint: "Hide for today" pauses these suggestions for 24 hours.

empty.title: No rules yet
empty.description: After every sync or import, a rule completes the transactions it targets: category, merchant, tag or name.

rules.disabled: Rule disabled. Transactions it already changed stay as they are.

form.description: After every sync or import, the rule applies to the transactions that meet all its conditions. With no condition, it applies to all of them. After saving, you can apply it to existing transactions.

form.effectiveDateHint: Optional. The rule only touches transactions dated on or after this day.
form.noCondition: No condition: the rule applies to all transactions.

recurring.title: Recurring transactions
recurring.description: Subscriptions, bills and income that come back on a regular rhythm, to within a few cents. Archant finds them in the last three months of transactions and suggests them as possible bills.

info.title: Automatic pattern detection
info.manual: You can identify patterns or clean up stale recurring transactions with the buttons above.
info.cleanup: "Clean stale" makes a recurring transaction inactive when it has gone without payment for two of its due dates, after two months at the earliest, or six for one added by hand.

triggers.import: after an import or its cancellation;

manage.title: Your bills are on the Bills page

assistants.title: AI assistants
assistants.description: Let Claude Code, VS Code or Cursor read your accounts and, if you allow it, categorize your transactions. Each assistant connects with your consent and disconnects in one click.

disconnectDialog.title: Disconnect {{name}}?

members.title: Members
members.description: The people who have access to Archant. An invited person chooses their own password from the link you send them.

promoteDialog.title: Make {{name}} an admin?
promoteDialog.description: {{name}} will be able to change everything, invite and remove members, and connect assistants. The change applies from their next action.

demoteDialog.description: {{name}} will be able to read everything without changing anything. Their connected assistants and pending invitations will be deleted.

removeDialog.description: {{name}} will no longer have access to Archant: their sessions will be closed on all their devices. The household's accounts and transactions stay.

members.removed: {{name}} no longer has access to Archant.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke the invitation for {{email}}?
revokeDialog.description: Their link will stop working right away. You can invite this address again.

empty.title: No pending invitations

inviteDialog.description: Archant does not send emails. You will copy a link and send it yourself.

general.title: General

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.subtitle: Customize how transactions are displayed

investments.title: Investments
investments.description: Prices of the securities you hold, to value your investment accounts without entering them.

fetch.title: Price fetching
fetch.label: Fetch prices every day
fetch.disclosure: When enabled, Archant requests prices from Yahoo Finance ({{host}}) on the first visit of the day and when you update them. Yahoo therefore learns which securities the household holds: Archant sends their ticker, never a quantity or an amount. Searching for a security also sends it the text you typed.
fetch.off: When disabled, no request leaves the server: investment accounts are valued from the balances you enter.

data.title: Data
data.description: Download everything Archant holds as a ZIP archive, in Sure's export format. Your data is never locked in here.

holds.title: What the archive contains
holds.accounts: Your accounts, their daily balances and your loan details
holds.transactions: Your transactions, with their category, merchant, tags and notes
holds.transfers: Your transfers, and the pairs you rejected

leavesOut.title: What it leaves out
leavesOut.secrets: Your password, sessions, keys and tokens
leavesOut.banks: Your bank connections and the identity of the bank's accounts
leavesOut.settings: Your settings and the assistants' log
leavesOut.replacements: Rules that only replace text in the name, which Sure cannot read

data.sign: In the archive, amounts follow Sure's sign: a purchase is positive and income is negative, the opposite of Archant. Balances, snapshots and budgets keep their sign.
data.notBackup: The archive contains your amounts and names in clear text: keep it somewhere safe. It is not a backup: Archant reads its all.ndjson back in "Imports", but without your passwords or your bank connections. To restore Archant, use a copy of the database.
